content:
We would like to introduce ReasLab IDE, a collaborative, cloud-based platform for exploring, verifying, and writing mathematical proofs in Lean 4.

(Web rendered version of this post)

It runs entirely in your browser, requiring no installation or download. All data is saved and synced in the cloud automatically.

Open ReasLab IDE

(You can try importing the Mathematics in Lean template)

Key Features

  • Zero-Install Environment: Get started instantly in the browser, with a file tree, editor tabs, and a Lean 4 Infoview.
  • Cloud Project Management: Work with different Lean 4 versions across projects, create new Lean projects using your preferred Lean version, import existing projects from GitHub, or start from templates.
  • Document Rendering: Built-in support for rendering LaTeX, Typst and Markdown directly in the IDE, allowing you to maintain both informal explanations and formal proofs in a unified workflow.
  • Real-Time Collaboration: Work on formal projects with your team in real-time. Similar to Overleaf for LaTeX, you can see edits from other users as they happen and navigate to their editing position.

Planned Features

We are working on:

  • LLM agent workflows similar to Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Claude Code, with GUI in the IDE
  • API documentation generation for your Lean projects hosted on the IDE (similar to mathlib4 docs) and integration
  • Blueprint project support for large-scale formalization efforts

Some of these features are already available in our internal testing preview version. If you are interested in early access, please feel free to contact us.

We built ReasLab to make formal methods more accessible and collaborative. For more details, see our documentation.

We welcome your feedback.
